formation.explanation: A client proposal allocates its origin row slot and establishes command/Seq/Deps at its owner. PreAccept receivers qualify ballot and merge local conflicts, reporting current value ballot and status. Matching replies supply the fast threshold; initial ballot plus equality and large-N committed-dependency conditions permit direct commit, otherwise Accept is broadcast and matching majority replies commit. Commit propagates the full tuple. Execution waits for committed dependency graph and orders SCCs before application and default client response.

context.explanation: Authority is per instance, not solely the master-selected leader. Initial ballot equals origin replica; recovery replaces leader bookkeeping and chooses a ballot based on proposer id and, when IsLeader, maxRecvBallot. Prepare raises the local promise and returns prior value ballot/status; formation rejects older requests and reply handlers qualify lastTriedBallot/phase. Execution detects incomplete work and queues recovery. Prepare quorum selection adopts highest value-ballot record and chooses committed installation, Accept, or restarted phase1; old client proposals are retained. Already committed records resist subsequent Accept and Commit replacement.

connection.explanation: Formation writes the same tuple and status that Prepare exposes to new owners. bal qualifies old requests while vbal and Status determine how old support is interpreted during recovery. Acks can contribute to local commit even though the receiver Accept path does not change Status; this discrepancy is retained rather than assuming an acceptance guarantee. Commit and execution establish prior decisions that restrict later handlers. Per-message delay goroutines mean pending messages can overlap authority changes; no FIFO handler-delivery assumption is used.
